item.title: ‘Netanyahu is walking a fine line’: US warns Israel on Gaza ceasefire deal — report
item.description: A US official has warned Prime Minister Netanyahu that President Trump could take severe action if the Gaza ceasefire deal is undermined. This warning follows the Knesset's vote to advance bills annexing parts of the West Bank, which reportedly stunned US officials and Vice President Vance, who was visiting Israel.

item.title: White House East Wing demolished for Trump’s $300M ballroom – see photos
item.description: The East Wing of the White House is now rubble. Donald Trump's new ballroom project is underway. This massive structure will cost $300 million. Funding comes entirely from private donors. Tech giants and prominent investors are contributing. Taxpayers will not bear any cost for this significant White House upgrade.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Dubai opens retail leasing inside metro and tram stations: How can businesses apply
item.description: Dubai's RTA is opening retail and commercial leasing opportunities within metro and tram stations to boost economic activity and commuter convenience. Businesses can now apply online for spaces, including 40 retail outlets and five sales kiosks along the Route 2020 extension, aiming to stimulate domestic trade and attract private investment.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE’s haunted Al Qasimi Palace up for sale: Would you buy this spooky mansion for AED 25 million?
item.description: Ras Al Khaimah's infamous "haunted" mansion, Al Qasimi Palace, is now for sale at AED 25 million, exclusively to Emirati nationals. Originally built in 1985 for over AED 500 million, the opulent palace was never occupied due to family objections. After restoration, it reopened as a cultural attraction, drawing visitors with its folklore and unique architecture.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Do you intend to overthrow the government?’ — Viral video revisits Indian emperor’s encounter with England’s first visitors
item.description: Irish comedy trio Foil Arms and Hog's Instagram sketch humorously reimagines the first meeting between an Indian emperor and English visitors. The skit cleverly flips the colonial power dynamic, presenting a modern immigration interview scenario. Viewers are praising the piece for its witty satire and ironic commentary on historical power plays disguised as polite conversation.
item.dc:creator: TOI Trending Desk

item.title: British-Palestinian doctor accused of backing October 7 Hamas attack wears gold necklace with number 7, faces backlash: 'Racist, anti-semite'
item.description: An NHS doctor, Rahmeh Aladwan, faces a Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service hearing over allegations of antisemitism and praising the October 7 Hamas attacks. She previously faced similar claims but was cleared. Aladwan, who denies wrongdoing, was recently arrested on suspicion of inciting racial hatred. The tribunal will decide on potential interim restrictions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: China and Russia reportedly using ‘sex warfare’ to spy on Silicon Valley; Elon Musk reacts
item.description: Chinese and Russian operatives are reportedly employing "sex warfare" to infiltrate Silicon Valley, using personal relationships to extract sensitive trade secrets and intellectual property. This human intelligence strategy targets emotional vulnerabilities, posing a significant threat to national security and the tech industry's openness. Experts warn of a growing pattern of such espionage.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: “How is she not canceled”: Viewers react to Nina Lin’s controversial IRL stream
item.description: A resurfaced clip of streamer Nina Lin has sparked outrage, showing her assistant allegedly being subjected to sexual acts despite objections. Viewers decry the incident as a double standard, demanding accountability. Lin denies wrongdoing, claiming the situation was taken out of context, further fueling criticism over consent and gender bias in streaming.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: California crash: Footage shows moment when Indian-origin truck driver 'rammed' into traffic; 3 killed
item.description: An Indian national, Jashanpreet Singh, is accused of causing a fatal multi-vehicle crash on a California freeway while allegedly under the influence of drugs. Federal immigration officials stated Singh is an illegal migrant who entered the U.S. in 2022 and was released into the country. The incident resulted in three deaths and several injuries.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: How OnlyFans beat Nvidia and Apple to become the world’s most revenue-efficient company
item.description: OnlyFans has become the world's most revenue-efficient company, generating $37.6 million per employee. The UK-based platform allows creators to monetize exclusive content directly from fans, reporting $1.41 billion in net revenue for fiscal year 2024. This success stems from its asset-light model, relying on user-generated content and a lean workforce.
item.dc:creator: TOI Business Desk

item.title: Resurfaced clip of Nina Lin sparks debate over sexual consent in streaming
item.description: A resurfaced May 2024 IRL stream featuring Nina Lin has sparked debate over sexual consent, showing Lin restraining Said while Zoe Spencer engaged in sexual acts. Viewers noted Said's attempts to leave, raising concerns about consent in public streams and whether male victims are taken seriously. Lin denied assault, calling it "embarrassing" for a man to report it.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Democrats urge Donald Trump to stay home amid government shutdown as White House confirms meeting with China's Xi Jinping
item.description: Amidst a prolonged government shutdown, Democrats are urging President Trump to cancel his upcoming Asia trip, including a meeting with China's Xi Jinping. Critics argue the President should prioritize domestic issues and the suffering of Americans over international diplomacy. Past presidents have canceled foreign travel during similar crises, a precedent Democrats hope Trump will follow.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Siddhartha Patel Daswani: 17-year-old Indian-American fighting wildfires with AI
item.description: A 17-year-old Indian-origin student, Siddhartha Patel Daswani, is revolutionizing wildfire prevention with AI. His initiative, SmokeSignal, uses advanced tools to detect and predict fires in real-time, offering crucial early warnings. Beyond technology, Daswani champions youth education and policy advocacy, planting trees and inspiring global climate action.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UK PM Keir Starmer pledges £10m to protect Muslims from hate crimes, faces backlash; 'what about churches?'
item.description: Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced an additional £10 million for mosque security following a suspected arson attack. This funding will enhance protective measures like CCTV and fencing for Muslim communities facing rising hate crimes. While lauded by Muslim groups, some social media users criticized the move, citing concerns about extremism and prioritizing specific communities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Justin Trudeau would 'never date a civilian,' say sources as ex-Canadian PM’s intimate photos with Katy Perry go viral
item.description: Former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau's new romance with pop star Katy Perry has surprised many, though sources close to him say it reflects his lifelong attraction to fame, similar to his father. The pair were photographed together, sparking speculation of a midlife crisis and a desire for fun after recent personal and professional challenges.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Abu Dhabi Police respond to rumours of ‘red pills’ in schools and universities on social media
item.description: Amid circulating “red pills” rumours, Abu Dhabi Police have confirmed schools and universities remain safe, urging parents and institutions to stay vigilant. Highlighting youth vulnerability. Experts warn that adolescents are especially vulnerable, as traffickers increasingly disguise drugs in everyday items like energy drinks, chewing gum, and flavoured paper, making awareness and vigilance essential.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE: Sharjah to begin enforcing separate lanes for buses, trucks, and motorcycles starting November 1
item.description: Sharjah is introducing dedicated traffic lanes for motorcycles, heavy vehicles, and buses starting November 1, 2025, to enhance road safety and streamline traffic flow. New regulations specify lane usage for different vehicle types, with strict enforcement via smart monitoring systems and penalties under Federal Traffic Law.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Foes to friends: Eric Adams backs Andrew Cuomo to take on Zohran Mamdani in NYC race
item.description: In a surprising political maneuver, Mayor Eric Adams has endorsed former Governor Andrew Cuomo for mayor, aiming to counter the rise of Democratic Socialist Zohran Mamdani. This unlikely alliance seeks to unite traditional Democrats and moderates against Mamdani's progressive platform, with both men focusing on key voter demographics.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Watch: Louvre robbers make daring escape in broad daylight with $100 million worth of jewels
item.description: In a brazen daylight heist, thieves made off with $100 million in jewels from the Louvre, captured on video using a construction lift for a slow escape. Four suspects are being hunted after they cut through glass, bypassed alarms, and casually looted displays. The audacious robbery, which saw them drop a valuable crown, concluded with a scooter getaway.
